Copilot now spans five core tiers, and the headline monthly fees are unchanged from the pre-June structure – though GitHub has since layered on a sixth option above Pro+. Cline takes the opposite tack entirely: the extension itself is free and open source, and developers bring their own API key, paying the model provider directly with zero markup. For a developer who already has Anthropic or OpenAI API credits, Cline’s bring-your-own-key model can be dramatically cheaper than any subscription – at the cost of doing your own plumbing. [...] The premium-request model introduced in 2025 was the first crack in that simplicity. It created a two-speed system: unlimited basic completions, but a capped pool of “premium” interactions for the powerful chat and agent features. That was already a meaningful philosophical change – it acknowledged that not all AI requests cost the same to serve. The June 2026 move to token billing is the logical endpoint of that journey: a full admission that the cost of serving an AI request is variable, sometimes wildly so, and that pricing must track cost rather than hide it behind a flat fee.

At GitHub Copilot, our mission is to support all development workflows, from AI-assisted coding using inline suggestions to agent-first software engineering in the VS Code Agents window. ## How AI Is Transforming DevOps in 2026

Software development is changing rapidly. Traditional DevOps practices have already transformed the way organizations build, test, deploy, and monitor applications. Now, **Artificial Intelligence is becoming an important part of the DevOps lifecycle**.

In 2026, DevOps teams are moving beyond simple automation toward **AI-assisted and agentic DevOps workflows**. Developers and DevOps engineers can use AI to generate code, analyze pull requests, create infrastructure, troubleshoot pipelines, understand logs, manage work items, and automate repetitive operational tasks.

Microsoft is actively expanding AI capabilities across Azure DevOps, including AI-assisted code reviews, Copilot-powered workflows, Azure DevOps MCP Server capabilities, and AI-agent-based DevOps scenarios.

This evolution is creating a new skill set:

**DevOps + Cloud + Automation + AI**

Professionals who understand this combination can build faster, more reliable, and more intelligent software delivery pipelines.

From intelligent code reviews and security analysis to deployment recommendations, AI helps teams improve speed, consistency, and software quality. [...] ## AI Use Cases in Azure DevOps

 AI-Assisted Code Review

When a Pull Request is created, Azure Pipelines triggers an Azure Function that sends the code changes to Azure OpenAI. The AI reviews the code for quality, coding standards, error handling, security risks, and performance issues, then posts feedback directly to the PR.

 PR Summarization

AI generates a concise summary of large pull requests, highlighting key changes, affected components, and review focus areas, helping reviewers quickly understand the context.

 Automated Test Generation

Based on the modified code, AI suggests unit tests for uncovered scenarios, helping teams improve test coverage and software reliability.
